title: Mathematics
description: Numbers, shapes and fun problems to solve.

entries.title: Counting
entries.summary: Counting tells us how many things there are.
entries.body: When we count we say one number for each thing. Numbers help us know how many, in what order and how much more or less. Numbers are used everywhere - from counting sheep to telling the time.
facts: We can count forwards or backwards.

entries.title: Adding
entries.body: When we add we put two numbers together to find the total. If you have 3 apples and I give you 2 more, you have 5 apples. Adding is one of the four things we do with numbers.
facts: Addition helps us work out totals.
You can add numbers in any order: 2 + 3 is the same as 3 + 2.

entries.title: Shapes
entries.body: A circle is round and has no corners. A square has four equal sides. A triangle has three sides. A rectangle has four sides but they are not all the same length. Shapes can be 2D like a drawing or 3D like a box.
facts: A cone has a point and a round base.
A sphere is a perfectly round 3D shape.

entries.title: Telling the Time
entries.summary: A clock shows us the time of day.
entries.body: There are 60 seconds in a minute and 60 minutes in an hour. The short hand points to the hour and the long hand points to the minutes. There are 24 hours in a day.
facts: Half past seven means 30 minutes past seven.
A day has 24 hours and a year has 12 months.
The minute hand is the long one.

entries.title: Patterns
entries.summary: Patterns repeat in a predictable way.
entries.body: A pattern is something that repeats in an order. Red, blue, red, blue is a pattern. Patterns help us work out what comes next, and you can find them in floor tiles, music, animals and the stars.
facts: You can find patterns in the spirals of shells.
Patterns help your brain to learn new things faster.

entries.title: Measuring
entries.summary: Measuring tells us how big, long or heavy something is.
entries.body: We measure with rulers, scales, tape measures and clocks. In the old days people measured with their hands, feet and body parts, which is why an inch was once called a thumb.
facts: You need a scale to measure weight and a ruler for length.

questions.prompt: How many sides does a triangle have?
questions.explanation: A triangle has three sides and three corners.

questions.prompt: How many minutes are in an hour?
questions.explanation: There are 60 minutes in an hour.
A circle is completely round with no corners.

questions.prompt: How many faces does a cube have?
questions.explanation: A cube has six square faces.

questions.prompt: Adding 2 and 3 gives the same answer as adding 3 and 2.
What do we use to measure length?
questions.explanation: A ruler or tape measure is used for length.

questions.prompt: In the pattern ABAB, what comes after AB?
questions.explanation: The pattern repeats, so after AB comes AB again.

questions.prompt: How many hours are in a full day?
questions.explanation: There are 24 hours in a day.
